subject: general
question: In which year did the government of India launch the Aatma Nirbhar Bharat Campaign?
solution:
The correct answer is __**2020**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Aatma Nirbhar Bharat Abhiyan (Self-Reliant India Campaign) was launched by the Indian government in **May 2020**.
 
• It aimed to make India self-reliant by promoting local manufacturing, supply chains, and innovation.
 
• The campaign was introduced as a response to the economic impact of the **COVID-19 pandemic**.
 
• The government announced a **₹20 lakh crore economic package** (equivalent to 10% of India's GDP) under this initiative.
 
• The campaign focuses on five pillars: **Economy, Infrastructure, System, Vibrant Demography, and Demand**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Aatma Nirbhar Bharat Package:**

 
 
• The package was announced in five tranches, focusing on sectors such as MSMEs, agriculture, health, and education.
 
• Measures included credit guarantees, tax reliefs, and direct benefit transfers to support businesses and individuals.
 
• Special focus was given to promoting local industries under the "Vocal for Local" initiative.
 
 
 
• **Reforms under the Campaign:**
 
 
• Structural reforms in agriculture, labor laws, and public sector enterprises were introduced.
 
• FDI limits in defense manufacturing were increased to promote domestic production.
 
• Focus was laid on enhancing the ease of doing business in India.
 
 
 
• **Key Sectors Targeted:**
 
 
• Healthcare: Strengthening healthcare infrastructure and promoting indigenous production of medical equipment.
 
• Agriculture: Enhancing supply chain efficiency and improving market access for farmers.
 
• Technology: Boosting digital infrastructure and promoting startups in tech-driven sectors.
 
 
 
• **Impact and Vision:**
 
 
• The initiative aims to reduce import dependency and position India as a global manufacturing hub.
 
• It aligns with the vision of a $5 trillion economy by 2024-25.
 
• The campaign promotes sustainability, innovation, and economic resilience in the long run.
